paper.title: Effect of odour on prey pattern aversion in jumping spiders.
paper.abstract: Many animals defend themselves with toxic chemicals and use multimodal warning displays involving odours and bright colours to advertise their toxicity. Yet, how coloration and odour interact and why they so often evolve together is not well understood. Recent work in jumping spiders has shown that defensive odours from three chemically defended bugs (Order Hemiptera: Acanthocephala femorata, Mormidea sp. and Leptoglossus phyllopus) increase a foraging aversion to red prey. Here, we ask whether these odours also increase avoidance of another visual warning: high-contrast stripes. Jumping spiders (Habronattus trimaculatus) were given choices between pattern-manipulated termites (solid white and black-and-white striped) in the presence or absence of a defensive odour from one of the aforementioned bug species. We predicted that any aversion to stripes would be stronger when odour was present. Surprisingly, we found no effect of any bug odour on the spiders' aversions to stripes. Interestingly, these odours that so strongly and consistently trigger aversion to red do not have the same effect on stripes. This highlights the different ways that odours and coloration can interact (or not) to influence predators, providing insight into the diversity of aposematic displays in nature.

paper.title: Altitude-induced plasticity of respiratory central-peripheral chemoreflex interaction.
paper.abstract: Stable breathing depends on the integrated action of central and peripheral chemoreceptors, but the nature of this interaction in humans and its physiological importance remain controversial. Previous studies reported additive, hypo-additive and hyper-additive responses across species, preparations and protocols. Here, we used a novel method to quantify peripheral chemoreflex sensitivity across graded levels of central chemoreceptor activation to test whether central-peripheral chemoreceptor interaction in awake humans is fixed or state dependent. At low altitude, the form of interaction varied across individuals, with most showing additive responses (12/17) and a substantial subset showing hypo-additivity (5/17). After 7-10 days of acclimatization to 3500 m, all five hypo-additive individuals became additive, and four additive participants became hyper-additive. This shift in interaction towards hyper-additivity provides the first evidence that central-peripheral chemoreceptor integration is plastic. Plasticity during wakefulness was not associated with individual differences in central sleep apnoea severity at high altitude. Thus, our findings confirm that central-peripheral chemoreceptor interaction differs among individuals and suggest that the form of interaction can be reshaped by hypobaric hypoxic stress. KEY POINTS: How central and peripheral chemoreceptor drives to breathe interact in humans and whether this process is plastic remains uncertain. We quantified peripheral chemoreflex sensitivity to hypoxia (PChS) across graded levels of central chemoreceptor activation at low altitude and after 7-10 days of high-altitude exposure (3500 m). Seventeen participants performed repeated modified rebreathing tests with end-tidal P O 2   fixed at 150 (hyperoxia), 60 and 45 mmHg (hypoxia). PChS was computed at 1 mmHg intervals of end-tidal P C O 2    ( P ETC O 2    ) from linear regression of the difference in ventilation between hypoxic and hyperoxic conditions vs. calculated arterial oxygen saturation (ScO2) (L·min-1·mmHg-1·%ScO2 -1). At low altitude, PChS increased with P ETC O 2    in all individuals; the relationship was linear (no interaction) in 12 participants, and 5 showed hypo-additivity. After acclimatization, central and peripheral chemoreflex sensitivities increased. All hypo-additive individuals became additive; four additive individuals became hyper-additive. Central-peripheral chemoreceptor interaction is plastic in humans and can shift towards hyper-additivity with sustained hypobaric hypoxia.

paper.title: Electronic patient-reported outcome monitoring and quality of life during later-line nivolumab therapy for advanced gastric cancer.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) often deteriorates during later-line treatment for advanced gastric cancer. Although nivolumab monotherapy has been an established treatment option in this setting, HRQoL data remain limited. This study aimed to examine associations between symptomatic adverse events (AEs) and HRQoL deterioration and to evaluate the feasibility of home-based electronic patient-reported outcome (ePRO) monitoring.

METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled patients aged ≥ 20 years with an ECOG performance status of 0-2 who were scheduled to receive later-line nivolumab monotherapy in clinical practice. Patients self-reported symptomatic AEs using PRO-CTCAE and assessed HRQoL weekly using FACT-Ga via a smartphone-based ePRO system for 12 weeks. The association between symptom deterioration and HRQoL decline was analyzed using a general linear model. Digital literacy and impressions of ePRO were also surveyed.

RESULTS: Among 29 evaluable patients, 20 completed the 12-week monitoring period. Median time to HRQoL deterioration was 9 weeks. Several symptomatic AEs, including stomatitis, dysgeusia, pain, malaise, and depression, showed nominal associations with HRQoL decline in unadjusted exploratory analyses (all nominal p < 0.05). Despite 37.9% of patients not regularly using smartphones, adherence to ePRO reporting was high, with only 0.95% missing data.

CONCLUSIONS: Exploratory analyses suggested potential associations between specific symptomatic AEs and HRQoL deterioration during later-line nivolumab therapy for advanced gastric cancer. ePRO monitoring achieved high data completeness, although patient acceptability was limited. These findings support further evaluation of ePRO as a tool for timely symptom recognition, alongside strategies to improve acceptability.

paper.title: The first comprehensive analysis of the flavor of Freekeh: a toasted, smoked, green durum wheat product, by analytical and sensory approaches.
paper.abstract: Freekeh, smoked immature durum wheat, has gastronomic significance and attractive nutritional values, fueling increasing global demand. Genotype and toasting intensity similarly play a pivotal role in shaping flavor. This study serves as the inaugural roadmap to freekeh flavor, establishing a predictive chemical/sensory framework uncovering novel cereal flavors, and providing producers benchmarks to fine-tune quality using early-harvest practices.

paper.title: Depression in the prodromal phase of Parkinson's disease: Clinical manifestations, biomarker evidence, and predictive implications.
paper.abstract: Depression is one of the earliest and most frequent non-motor symptoms in the prodromal phase of Parkinson's disease (PD), often preceding motor signs by years to decades. This review synthesizes epidemiological, neuroimaging, biomarker, and genetic evidence to clarify whether depression is a risk factor, a direct prodromal manifestation, or both. Meta-analyses consistently show a two-fold increased risk of subsequent PD in individuals with depressive symptoms or major depressive disorder (MDD), with the highest risk occurring within 1-2 years of diagnosis but persisting for up to 25 years. Late-onset depressive syndrome (after age 50-60) is associated with dopaminergic deficits on dopamine transporter imaging in 24-79% of cases, supporting it as a prodromal symptom, whereas early-onset depression may act through shared genetic vulnerability or chronic inflammatory pathways. Neuroimaging in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) reveals that depression correlates with caudate atrophy, frontostriatal white matter disruption, and brainstem monoaminergic dysfunction, but not simply with nigrostriatal denervation. Depression frequently coexists with RBD, autonomic dysfunction, and olfactory impairment, likely reflecting shared brainstem pathology. Genetic forms of PD (GBA1, SNCA, LRRK2, PRKN) show variable depression prevalence, providing mechanistic insights into lysosomal, inflammatory, and proteostatic pathways. Emerging evidence implicates IL-17A, sIL-2R, and α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregation as convergent points linking depression and prodromal α-synucleinopathy, with gut-brain axis dysfunction potentially amplifying this process. Current Movement Disorder Society prodromal PD criteria include depression but have limited sensitivity in general populations. No disease-modifying trials have tested whether treating prodromal depression alters phenoconversion risk. We conclude that proximal, late-onset depressive syndrome is a robust prodromal marker, while distant or early-onset depression, including MDD, identifies a chronically elevated risk population. Future studies should integrate multimodal biomarkers and test therapeutic interventions in prodromal cohorts.

paper.title: Development and Validation of the 9-item Parkinson's Disease Screening Questionnaire.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to develop and validate a brief, self-administered questionnaire integrating motor and prodromal non-motor symptoms for screening Parkinson's disease (PD).

METHODS: We conducted a three-phase study. Phase 1 used a prospectively registered systematic review of 107 studies to generate a 52-item draft. In Phase 2, the draft was refined in 205 participants (122 with early PD and 83 healthy controls) using item-level areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) and age- and sex-adjusted multivariable logistic regression. Phase 3 validated the 9-item Korean PD Screening Questionnaire (KPDSQ) in an independent cohort (n = 246; 122 PD, 45 essential tremor [ET], and 79 controls), and included a 4-week test-retest reassessment.

RESULTS: The final 9-item KPDSQ comprises seven motor items (rest tremor, shuffling or short-step gait, slow daily activities, decreased arm swing, soft voice, masked face, and freezing of gait) and two non-motor items (hyposmia and dream-enactment behavior). At a cutoff of ≥2, sensitivity was 88.5% and specificity was 92.4% for distinguishing PD from controls (AUC = 0.970; 95% CI, 0.946-0.984; p < 0.001). At ≥3, the KPDSQ distinguished PD from ET (AUC = 0.774; 95% CI, 0.680-0.847; p < 0.001). Internal consistency was high (Cronbach's α = 0.800), test-retest reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.921), and scores correlated with MDS-UPDRS Part III scores in patients with PD (Spearman's ρ = 0.330; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The 9-item KPDSQ is a reliable, clinically valid screening tool combining motor and prodromal non-motor features. Prospective community-based validation is warranted.

paper.title: Treatment of Frey's Syndrome With "Ready to Use Liquid" Relabotulinumtoxin A (Relfydess).
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the off-label intradermal use of ready-to-use liquid relabotulinumtoxinA (Relfydess) for symptomatic Frey's syndrome after parotidectomy.

METHODS: A 72-year-old man with gustatory sweating and flushing after total parotidectomy and adjuvant radiotherapy, who had previously responded to conventional botulinum toxin A, underwent gustatory provocation, clinical mapping, and intradermal relabotulinumtoxinA injections using a 1-cm2 grid. Clinical response and treatment-related adverse events were assessed at 6 weeks and 3 months.

RESULTS: At 6 weeks and 3 months, the patient reported symptom reduction comparable to his previous treatment with conventional botulinum toxin A. At 3 months, repeat gustatory stimulation elicited no visible sweating. No treatment-related adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSION: In this patient, ready-to-use liquid relabotulinumtoxinA provided sustained symptom control for 3 months without observed adverse events. This formulation may offer a practical off-label option for previously responsive patients, while product-specific potency units should not be considered interchangeable.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 5.

paper.title: Longitudinal olfactory and neuropsychological trajectories across the GBA1 spectrum.
paper.abstract: Tracking non-motor symptoms and neuropsychological function is critical for assessing neurodegenerative progression. We characterized differences among individuals with Gaucher disease, GBA1 variant carriers and GBA1-associated Parkinson disease to identify candidate markers of Parkinson disease-related change in Gaucher disease or GBA1 variant carriers. We analysed data from 161 adults evaluated at the National Institutes of Health between 1983 and 2024, including 79 with Gaucher disease, 52 GBA1 variant carriers and 30 with GBA1-associated Parkinson disease. Assessments included questionnaires for non-motor symptoms, depression, anxiety, fatigue, sleepiness, olfaction and intelligence quotient measures. Eighty-seven participants contributed longitudinal data from at least two visits. Linear mixed-effects models, adjusted for age, sex and education, examined baseline differences and longitudinal trajectories. At baseline, the GBA1-associated Parkinson disease group showed lower olfactory performance (compared with both groups, P < 0.0001), greater daytime sleepiness (compared with GBA1 variant carriers, P = 0.003; compared with Gaucher disease, P = 0.0002) and higher non-motor symptom burden (compared with both groups, P < 0.0001). Only olfaction declined longitudinally, most steeply in GBA1-associated Parkinson disease (P < 0.0001; rate: 0.65 points per year, P = 0.032). In this longitudinal cohort, olfactory decline was the most robust marker differentiating GBA1-associated Parkinson disease from Gaucher disease and GBA1 variant carriers. Intelligence quotient and non-motor symptom measures did not demonstrate a comparable decline, reflecting their limited sensitivity to longitudinal change, and reinforcing the need for objective, biologically based measures. Among participants without Parkinson disease at study onset, test scores remained stable over follow-up and phenoconversion was rare, underscoring the very low observed Parkinson disease penetrance among individuals with biallelic or heterozygous GBA1 variants.

paper.title: OLFM4 promotes intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma progression through a PKM2-glycolysis-histone lactylation feedback loop.
paper.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming is increasingly recognized as a key characteristic of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) initiation and progression. Among these metabolic alterations, glycolysis is central for supporting tumor growth. Elucidating the precise molecular mechanisms of glycolysis in ICC is critical for developing precision therapies. Here, comprehensive integrative analyses revealed that olfactomedin 4 (OLFM4) is upregulated in ICC specimens and is associated with adverse patient outcomes. Mechanistically, OLFM4 promotes ICC progression by recruiting ubiquitin specific peptidase 10 (USP10) to stabilize pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2). This interaction enhances glycolysis and lactate production, thereby elevating histone lactylation, with a prominent impact on H3K18 lactylation (H3K18la). Consequently, H3K18la positively regulates OLFM4 transcription, establishing a positive glycolysis-histone lactylation feedback loop. Notably, tiliroside, a candidate pharmacological inhibitor of OLFM4, demonstrated antitumor efficacy in ICC. Collectively, these findings support targeting OLFM4 as a promising therapeutic strategy for ICC management.

paper.title: Neural responses to food-related stimuli following experimental sleep manipulation: A systematic review of task-based neuroimaging studies.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adequate sleep is essential for physiological, cognitive, and mental functioning. While epidemiological and behavioral studies show that sleep restriction or sleep deprivation is associated with altered responses to food stimuli, the neural mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. The preregistered systematic review synthesized evidence from task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging studies examining neural responses to food-related stimuli following experimental sleep manipulations, including sleep deprivation or sleep restriction.

METHOD: Literature searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and American Psychological Association PsycInfo, yielding 11 eligible studies, including nine with adult samples and two with adolescent samples. We extracted the data, assessed the risk of bias, and conducted a qualitative synthesis.

RESULTS: Across studies with adult samples, six visual food-cue studies generally reported stronger brain activity following sleep deprivation or sleep restriction, particularly in the striatum, insula, anterior cingulate cortex, and inferior frontal gyrus. Two food valuation studies, including a willingness-to-pay and food-desire task, showed enhanced neural activity in the amygdala and hypothalamus during food valuation. Moreover, one study using a food odor perception paradigm showed that sleep deprivation altered chemosensory and interoceptive processing by enhancing food odor encoding in the piriform cortex. Two adolescent studies reported distinct neural findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Together, these findings highlight that experimentally induced sleep deprivation or sleep restriction does not uniformly enhance reward-related brain activity; rather, it is associated with task-dependent changes in neural responses to food-related stimuli. However, the limited and heterogeneous evidence limits conclusions regarding common neural mechanisms. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

paper.title: Gastric Mixed Neuroendocrine-Non-neuroendocrine Neoplasms Develop from POU2F3+ Multipotent Progenitors.
paper.abstract: Gastric mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) are aggressive malignancies that exhibit complex cellular heterogeneity driven by the dual lineages. The dismal patient survival rates highlight the need to elucidate the cellular origin of gastric MiNENs and the key regulatory mechanisms to develop improved treatment strategies. Here, we identified a gastric POU2F3+epithelial population as a potential cell of origin for gastric MiNENs. Lineage tracing and single-cell RNA sequencing further identified that POU2F3+ cells include three distinct subpopulations with divergent differentiation trajectories: progenitor cells (SOX2+SOX9+), tuft cells (POU2F3+DCLK1+), and neuroendocrine cells (SYP+CHGA+). Combined Rb1/Trp53 deletion and MYC overexpression in POU2F3+ epithelial cells (Pou2f3-CreERT; Rb1fl/fl; Trp53fl/fl; LSL-MycT58A) led to the rapid development of gastric MiNENs containing both neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine lesions, recapitulating human gastric MiNENs pathology. Transcription factor activity analysis and spatial transcriptomics revealed SOX2 and SOX9 as critical regulators driving subpopulation specification, with SOX2 and SOX9 being enriched in dysplasia and adenocarcinoma, respectively. Bulk RNA sequencing further showed increased expression of CXCL5 in gastric MiNENs, and inhibition of CXCL5 reduced the growth of tumor organoids and xenografts in mouse models. Together these findings offer a physiologically relevant model for studying gastric MiNENs and identify CXCL5 as a potential therapeutic target for this heterogeneous cancer.

paper.title: Concentration-dependent modulation of the aroma profile of Jiang-flavor Baijiu by isoamyl alcohol through noncovalent interactions with key aroma compounds.
paper.abstract: Isoamyl alcohol (IAA), a key higher alcohol in Baijiu, is capable of both enhancing and disrupting aroma balance depending on its concentration. This study investigates its concentration-dependent role using recombination models with quantitative descriptive analysis, molecular dynamics simulations and 1H NMR spectroscopy. At 200-400 mg/L, IAA enhanced floral and fruity aromas while suppressing acidic and roasted aroma, consistent with reduced compound volatility. Above 600 mg/L, the inhibitory effect on aroma release weakened. These concentration-dependent effects on aroma are driven by changes in compound volatility mediated by hydrogen bond, with van der Waals and Coulomb interactions contributing. 1H NMR confirmed hydrogen bonding between IAA and aroma compounds via 0.05-0.09 ppm downfield shifts. Notably, the 400-650 mg/L range represents a pivotal transition window for sensory traits, compound volatility and hydrogen bond formation with IAA. However, a limitation remains in fully bridging the nonlinear gap between microscopic molecular interactions and human olfactory perception, as in vivo sensory integration involves complex perceptual mechanisms beyond physical volatility modulation.

paper.title: Influence of different cell wall disruption methods on flavor quality of yeast extract: mechanistic insights through peptidomics and molecular docking.
paper.abstract: Yeast extract (YE) is a widely used natural flavor enhancer whose taste and aroma quality govern its industrial value. However, how the cell wall disruption method, the first and decisive step of YE production, shapes flavor at the molecular level remains unclear, leaving method selection largely empirical. In this study, five representative disruption methods, autolysis (AY), ethyl acetate chemical disruption (EA), high-pressure homogenization (HPH), low-temperature colloid milling (LCM), and glucanase enzymatic hydrolysis (GE), were systematically compared using sensory evaluation, electronic nose and tongue, free amino acid and nucleotide profiling, solvent-assisted flavor evaporation coupled with gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (SAFE-GC-O-MS), electroencephalography (EEG), liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) peptidomics, and molecular docking. Results showed that GE produced the highest umami amino acid content (113.01 mg/g DW, p < 0.05) and the lowest bitterness, whereas EA yielded the highest bitter amino acid proportion; SAFE-GC-O-MS identified 117 volatile compounds, of which 67 (odor activity value ≥1) drove inter-group differentiation, and peptidomics revealed 1785 differential peptides, with GE generating more glutamate/aspartate-rich umami-associated peptides. In addition, molecular docking demonstrated that GE-derived acidic peptides bound the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3 most strongly (ΔG down to -9.18 kcal/mol), whereas EA-derived hydrophobic peptides preferentially engaged the bitter receptors TAS2R13/TAS2R14; synthesized-peptide validation corroborated these predictions (r = 0.93). Therefore, entropy-weighted TOPSIS confirmed the ranking GE > LCM > HPH > EA > AY, and this study establishes a "disruption method to peptide profile to receptor selectivity to flavor quality" framework guiding the industrial production of high-quality YE.

paper.title: Machine learning coupled with quantum chemical and sensory validation: Mechanistic insight into flavor modulation of SeNP-enriched fermented cornelian cherry-yacon juice.
paper.abstract: Cornelian cherry (Cornus officinalis) is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb that was first recorded in Shennong Ben Cao Jing approximately 1800 years ago. It has long been highly valued for its tonifying and astringent properties (such as nourishing the liver and kidneys and helping to retain semen and reduce urinary leakage). Although it possesses both medicinal and edible value, its flavor-which is characterized by strong astringency and slight bitterness-limits its use in food. Lactic acid bacteria can convert inorganic selenium into organic selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs), which not only improve the unpleasant taste but also increase the bioavailability of the resulting SeNPs. This study combines response surface methodology (RSM) and machine learning (ML) with quantum chemical calculations and sensory validation for predictive quality control, with the aim of elucidating the molecular basis of flavor improvement. The fermentation conditions optimized via RSM were 33 °C, a mass ratio of 1:3 between cornelian cherry and yacon, and an enzyme dosage of 0.6 g/L. HS-GC-IMS analysis revealed that esters with fruity odor characteristics continued to accumulate during fermentation, whereas aldehyde levels tended to decrease. Nontargeted metabolomics further revealed that the phenylpropanoid metabolic pathway and tannin-related metabolites were downregulated overall, providing a metabolic explanation for the reduction in astringency. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicated that esters with lower ΔE bind less strongly to the bitter taste receptor TAS2R14 than aldehydes with higher ΔE. Concentration-response, equimolar comparison, and spike-back experiments confirmed the sensory contribution of ester accumulation to bitterness reduction, while molecular docking suggested potential involvement of TAS2R14. Among the ML models evaluated, the TabPFN - a transformer-based model requiring no hyperparameter tuning achieved the highest predictive accuracy for the comprehensive quality score (R2 = 0.928), outperforming XGBoost (R2 = 0.912) and RSM (R2 = 0.876). Offline multi-objective simulation suggested that batch-to-batch variability in DPPH scavenging could theoretically be reduced by 41.3% while maintaining a SeNP conversion of 89.4%. By dissecting the distinct mechanisms of astringency reduction (tannin degradation) and bitterness alleviation (low-ΔE ester/TAS2R14 modulation) and providing a deployable ML model, this work offers a transferable paradigm for the rational design of flavor-optimized functional fermented foods from medicinal and edible resources.

paper.title: Umami-active components in edible Fungi: Distribution, structure-function relationships, molecular mechanisms, computational insights and industrial applications.
paper.abstract: Edible mushrooms are a biodiverse yet underutilized source of umami compounds providing clean-label alternatives to synthetic flavourings such as monosodium glutamate (MSG). The characteristic savory taste arises from interactions among free amino acids (glutamate, aspartate), 5'-ribonucleotides (5'-GMP, 5'-IMP), organic acids (succinic, citric), polyols (trehalose, mannitol), and bioactive peptides, whose accumulation is influenced by genetic composition, growth substrate, developmental stage, and postharvest management. This review systematically examines the distribution of umami compounds in Pleurotus spp., Lentinula edodes, Hypsizygus marmoreus, and other species, with emphasis on umami peptides, their structure-function relationships, and taste perception mediated by T1R1/T1R3, mGluR1/mGluR4, and CaSR receptors. In addition, it critically assesses industrial applications and advanced computational approaches including iUmami-SCM, UMPred-FRL, Umami-MRNN, Umami-BERT, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations for high-throughput discovery of umami peptides. Enzymatic hydrolysis coupled with ultrafiltration enriches low-molecular-weight (<3 kDa) umami peptides while reducing associated bitterness. Equivalent Umami Concentration (EUC) reflects an 8-10-fold synergistic enhancement between amino acids and nucleotides, where the synergistic constant represents the strength of their non-additive umami interaction. While fungal peptides are highly valued for their unique sensory contributions, their significance extends beyond taste as they also exert multifunctional bioactivities including ACE inhibition (IC₅₀: 9-150 μM), antioxidant activity (DPPH and ABTS assays), and endothelial protection. Challenges include genetic engineering strategies for umami enhancement, salt-umami interactions, and analytical standards. Emerging industrial applications, including CRISPR/Cas9-based metabolic engineering and agro-waste upcycling, position edible fungi as promising platforms for clean-label flavor systems, sodium reduction, and circular food economies.

paper.title: A flavor-modification strategy for Pu-erh raw tea to selectively rebalance key aroma-taste drivers and improve drinking comfort based on supercritical CO2 technology.
paper.abstract: Flavor adjustment techniques have long been an essential topic in tea research, among them, supercritical CO₂ extraction (SFE-CO₂) remains insufficiently explored. This study aimed to evaluate the potential of SFE-CO₂ to reshape aroma-taste profiles of Pu-erh raw tea (RAPT). Two key control factors including cosolvent and rehydration pre-treatment were constructed, RAPT and five SFE treatments were compared. Sensory evaluation, HPLC-UV, targeted polyphenol analysis, untargeted volatile compound analysis, and odor activity value (OAV) were integrated to characterize sensory responses and chemical drivers. SFE treatments generally reduced bitterness, astringency, and aftertaste intensity, whereas umami and sweetness scores showed no significant differences among treatments. Major tea matrix constituents, including total polyphenols (19.75-20.28%) and total free amino acids (3.37-3.89%) remained stable, whereas caffeine decreased by up to 32.28%. Polyphenol monomers and volatiles analysis showed compositional rebalancing pattern rather than a global loss. Five polyphenol and six key volatiles were identified as markers for process monitoring (such as morin, luteolin, gallic acid, benzaldehyde, phenylacetaldehyde, β-cyclocitral and geraniol). Collectively, these results established a framework for SFE-enabled flavor improvement in tea.

paper.title: Flavor profile characterization and quality evaluation of ginger oils using GC-MS, intelligent sensory and molecular docking approaches.
paper.abstract: Ginger volatile oil is highly favored by consumers for its unique aroma, yet its key aroma components, perception mechanisms, and aroma quality evaluation methods remain insufficiently clarified. Herein, Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), intelligent sensory, and molecular docking were integrated to analyze the aroma characteristics of ginger volatile oils systematically. Ten potential key aroma components were identified via ROAV analysis to establish aroma fingerprints (similarity >0.9) for evaluating commercial samples. The quality discrepancies of ginger oils were mainly attributed to the absence and imbalance ratios of potential key aroma components, especially cineole, m-cymene and geraniol. Intelligent sensory parameters (W1S, W2S, W5C and a*) can serve as auxiliary indicators for quality evaluation. Molecular docking demonstrated that α-curcumene and β-phellandrene exhibited the strongest interactions with olfactory receptors (ORs) through hydrogen bonds and π-π interactions. This study achieved comprehensive aroma evaluation of ginger volatile oil and clarified the potential molecular interactions between its characteristic aroma components and ORs.

paper.title: Integrating instrumental analysis and computational simulation to elucidate the effect of dual-enzyme hydrolysis combined with γ-glutamylation on the flavor characteristics of soybean meal.
paper.abstract: To improve soybean meal's flavor, this study explored the effect and mechanism of dual-enzyme hydrolysis combined with γ-glutamylation on the flavor characteristics of soybean meal. Specifically, γ-glutamylation increased umami amino acid (18.23 mg/100 mL), reduced bitter amino acids (26.94 mg/100 mL). Meanwhile, it also elevated esters and heterocyclic compounds (P < 0.05). Correlation analysis showed umami/sweet amino acids were positively correlated with umami/kokumi (P < 0.05), with ethyl formate, 2,6- and 2,5-dimethylpyrazine as potential contributors Besides, γ-Glutamylation increased potential umami peptides by 16.70%, with 7-13 amino acid peptides dominating. Molecular docking identified key interaction modes (hydrogen bond, hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions) and residues (Asp216, Ser147, Ala302 for T1R1/T1R3; Asp215, Gln179, Ser147 for calcium-sensing receptor). This strategy effectively improves soybean meal's flavor, providing theoretical support for novel flavor base materials development.

paper.title: Host Volatiles Drive Host Preference and Consequently Shape the Fitness of a Generalist Parasitoid Wasp, Meteorus pulchricornis (Hymenoptera: Braconidae).
paper.abstract: Host preference is critical to the efficacy of parasitoids in biological control, while the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we found that the host preference of the generalist parasitoid Meteorus pulchricornis revealed an innate preference for Spodoptera frugiperda, followed by Plodia interpunctella. GC-MS analysis showed distinct volatile organic compound profiles between the two hosts, with 2-hexanol as a shared component. Electroantennogram (EAG) recordings showed that wasp antennae responded more strongly to S. frugiperda than to P. interpunctella odors, suggesting olfaction mediates host preference. Knockdown of the odorant receptor co-receptor, MpulORco, impaired both EAG responses and host preference behavior. Furthermore, wasps reared on S. frugiperda had larger body size and higher fecundity, providing a plausible fitness-based explanation for the observed preference. Collectively, our study reveals olfaction is involved in host preference behavior in a generalist parasitoid and establishes a functional connection between olfactory cues and individual fitness.

paper.title: The effect of azelastine on basal forced expiratory volume in one second in asthmatics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
paper.abstract: Nearly 5 to 10% of asthmatics show a problematic drug tachyphylaxis, featuring the need for new therapies. Bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) are expressed in the airway tract, and their activation leads to multiple antiasthma effects. Azelastine, an antihistaminic drug with a strong bitter taste, is used to treat allergic rhinitis but is frequently prescribed for asthma. The present study aims to evaluate the bronchodilator effect of azelastine in asthmatic patients. We searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Scopus databases from inception to April 1, 2026. Studies investigating the effect of azelastine on baseline forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of asthmatic patients, compared to a placebo, were included. Mean differences between the two arms were calculated using a random effects model. The systematic search retrieved 145 articles, of which 8 met the inclusion criteria. Azelastine improved FEV1 by 7.57% compared to placebo (p<0.001). The heterogeneity was low (I2=0%), and the overall methodological quality of the selected studies was high, except in four studies, where a risk of bias was observed due to deviations from the intended intervention. Meta-regression analysis showed no significant impact of age, sex ratio, and baseline FEV1 on the global effect size (p>0.05). Azelastine treatment improves FEV1 in asthmatic patients. These results support the previously reported bronchodilator benefits of azelastine through TAS2Rs activation. However, more clinical studies are still needed to explore the therapeutic potential of TAS2R-targeted treatments in asthma.

paper.title: Navigation-Guided Spatial Mapping of Subclinical Local Invasion in Sinonasal and Nasopharyngeal Malignancies.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclinical local invasion (SLI) beyond radiologically evident margins poses a major challenge in the management of sinonasal and nasopharyngeal malignancies (SNNM). The biological behavior underlying this phenomenon remains poorly characterized, particularly regarding its spatial extent and histology-dependent patterns.

METHODS: This prospective study included patients undergoing surgical resection of SNNM with intraoperative surgical navigation (SN). Intraoperative biopsies were systematically mapped and spatially correlated with preoperative imaging. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the association between positive biopsy probability, distance from the gross tumor surface, and histologic characteristics.

RESULTS: Fifty-four patients and 569 biopsies were analyzed; 78 (13.7%) were positive. A significant inverse association between distance from the gross tumor surface and positive biopsy probability was observed, with an approximately 5.1% reduction in odds per millimeter (p-value < 0.001). Histologic type remained independently associated with positive biopsy probability after distance adjustment (p-value < 0.001). Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC), squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) with perineural invasion (PNI), other poorly differentiated carcinomas (OPDC), and mesenchymal malignancies showed wider SLI, whereas SCC without PNI, intestinal-type adenocarcinoma (ITAC), and olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB) demonstrated limited SLI. Tissue-specific effects were generally limited, although neural tissue was associated with increased positive biopsy probability in ACC.

CONCLUSIONS: SLI in SNNM follows a distance-dependent pattern with the distance-invasion relationship varying according to histologic subtype. SN-based mapping represents a spatially informed strategy to enhance margin assessment and guide histology-driven surgical and radiotherapy planning.

KEY POINTS: Navigation-guided mapping helped to estimate microscopic tumor spread patterns. Subclinical infiltration probability decreases by approximately 5.1% per mm from the tumor margin. Histologic subtype influences the extent of microscopic local invasion. ACC showed the widest microscopic local invasion, followed by SCC with PNI. PNI increased the tumor spread in sinonasal squamous carcinoma.

paper.title: Widespread structural variations at human chromosome ends.
paper.abstract: The highly repetitive regions of the human genome were long underrepresented from reference assemblies, limiting study of their biological function. Long-read sequencing and improved assembly algorithms have since resolved many of these regions, from centromeres to ribosomal DNA arrays, revealing structural variation increasingly linked to human disease. However, the subtelomeres, the repeat-rich regions adjacent to the telomeres at each chromosome end, have remained poorly characterized. Here we present a collection of complete subtelomeric sequences spanning all non-acrocentric chromosome arms, derived from 860 haploid assemblies across six ancestry groups. We find that while subtelomeres are mosaics of blocks shared between chromosome arms, individual arms diverge extensively, such that most non-acrocentric autosomal arms (54%, 21 of 39) carry multiple haplotypes differing by up to 100-200 kb. These blocks are broadly conserved across the great apes. In humans, their diversity is associated with chromosome arm rather than ancestry, suggesting that cross-arm paralogy block duplications predate human population divergence, although some haplotypes show ancestry-specific enrichment. Remarkably, these divergent haplotypes differ in gene content, driving gene copy-number variation between individuals among olfactory receptors and other genes. This study also revealed rare subtelomeric recombination. We further show that our subtelomere data set enables the accurate measurement of telomere length at individual chromosome ends from long-read data. Together, these assemblies reveal an unappreciated scale of variation at human chromosome ends and provide a resource for studying the roles of this variation in disease, telomere biology and genome evolution across diverse populations.

paper.title: Case Report: When reflux smells like smoke: a case of phantosmia associated with gastroesophageal reflux.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phantosmia is the perception of an odor without an external stimulus. Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) has been associated with olfactory dysfunction, but phantosmia has rarely been described.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 40-year-old woman with longstanding GERD developed intermittent perceptions of cigarette smoke during a week of worsening heartburn and bloating. Episodes were accompanied by déjà vu, nausea, and chills. A double-contrast barium esophagram demonstrated a small hiatal hernia and reflux to the thoracic inlet. She reported approximately 80% improvement after starting omeprazole, with brief recurrence during a heartburn flare, and complete resolution at later follow-up. Migraine with aura, allergic rhinitis, focal seizures, and psychiatric causes were considered as alternative explanations.

CONCLUSION: The close relationship between reflux activity and olfactory symptoms, together with improvement during reflux-directed treatment, supports a plausible association between GERD and phantosmia. This single case does not establish causation, and neurologic and sinonasal etiologies should remain part of the evaluation.

paper.title: Impact of Whole Legume Flour Addition on the Physicochemical, Textural, and Sensory Properties of Greek Fermented Flatbread "Langites".
paper.abstract: Langites, a traditional flatbread made from a fermented batter baked at 210°C, was investigated regarding the effects of replacing wheat flour with whole-grain red lentil or chickpea flour on the physicochemical, structural, textural, and sensory properties of langites. Wheat flour was substituted with each legume flour at 0%, 10%, and 30%, and flour functionality and product quality were comprehensively evaluated. Both legume flours exhibited substantially coarser particle-size distributions than wheat flour, with median particle sizes (D50) of 321.2 μm for chickpea, compared with 122.5 μm for wheat flour. The incorporation of legume flours increased water absorption capacity, reaching 2.56 g/g for chickpea blends and 2.40 g/g for lentil blends, whereas higher water solubility was observed in lentil formulations (4.32%). Flour and product color changed significantly, with color differences (Δ E) reaching 23.57 for red lentil and 10.93 for chickpea flour. In langites, increasing legume substitution significantly increased moisture content, hardness, gumminess, and chewiness, whereas cohesiveness decreased from 0.85 to 0.80 in the 30% lentil formulation. Image analysis revealed a marked reduction in the number and uniformity of surface eyes, accompanied by an increase in mean eye diameter from 0.97 mm (control) to 1.29 mm and 1.14 mm in langites containing 30% lentil and chickpea flour, respectively, indicating impaired gluten development and reduced gas retention. Sensory evaluation showed that 10% substitution received good acceptability (7.26-7.59) compared with the wheat control (8.21), whereas 30% substitution significantly reduced acceptance, particularly for lentil flour (4.19). Principal component analysis demonstrated that overall acceptability was positively associated with eye number and sweet-taste perception and negatively associated with hardness, chewiness, larger irregular pores, and color intensity. Overall, the 10% substitution with whole-grain legume flour represents a promising formulation with enhanced nutritional value while preserving desirable technological and sensory characteristics.

paper.title: Gut microbiota-derived small molecules, peptides, and proteins in GPCR signaling: current evidence for β-arrestin involvement.
paper.abstract: Gut microbiota modulate host metabolism, immunity, barrier integrity, and neural function through diverse classes of molecules, including small molecules such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), bile acids, tryptophan metabolites, and microbe-derived peptides and proteins. G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute a major receptor system through which the host senses microbiota-derived signals. However, current research has largely focused on ligand recognition, G protein pathways and functional phenotypes, leaving an insufficient understanding of how signals are reorganized after receptor activation to generate functional selectivity. In addition to mediating GPCR desensitization and endocytosis, β-arrestin regulates receptor trafficking, sustains endosomal signaling, and orchestrates signaling scaffold assembly, thereby providing a key mechanistic framework for understanding the spatiotemporal reprogramming of microbiota-derived signaling. This review summarizes both canonical and non-canonical GPCR signaling mechanisms, delineates the roles of β-arrestin in regulating receptor fate, biased signaling, and functional outputs. By integrating the PRESTO-Tango system and the PubMed literature, we analyzed the microbiome-related evidence for the near-complete non-olfactory GPCRome (314 conventional GPCRs) in order to assess the association between distinct classes of microbiota-derived molecules and GPCR-β-arrestin signaling. Current evidence indicates that existing studies are dominated by small-molecule signals, whereas evidence for peptides and proteins remains relatively limited. Moreover, most functional studies cannot be directly interpreted as evidence for β-arrestin-dependent mechanisms. A β-arrestin-centered conceptual framework for GPCR signaling regulation may provide a basis forunderstanding how gut microbiota-associated molecules influence host physiological functions through thespatiotemporal modulation of receptor signaling.

paper.title: Integrative quality evaluation of tea raw material uniformity using sensory analysis, metabolomics, GC-O, and principal component analysis.
paper.abstract: Although mechanical harvesting reduces labor costs, non-selective picking decreases fresh leaf uniformity, increasing the difficulty of sorting and high-value processing. This study used sensory evaluation, metabolomics, gas chromatography-olfactometry, and principal component analysis (PCA) to investigate the effects of raw material uniformity (U1 ~ U5) on tea flavor. The results show that high uniformity materials (U1 ~ U2) have floral and green aromas, with a fresh and full-bodied taste, while low uniformity materials (U4 ~ U5) are enriched with mature woody, roasted, sweet aromas and sweetness. Bitterness, astringency, and umami decrease as uniformity declines. A total of 23 key flavor compounds were identified, and their content changes were mainly related to differences in leaf maturity and drying time. In addition, PCA revealed distinct distribution patterns between U1 ~ U3 and U4 ~ U5, supporting "one bud with three leaves" as the sorting threshold between medium- and low-grade mechanically harvested fresh tea leaves.

paper.title: Cholera toxin remodels intestinal immunity and suppresses systemic metabolism.
paper.abstract: Cholera toxin (CTx) is a potent enterotoxin and widely used mucosal adjuvant, yet the acute host response to CTx itself, in the absence of a co-administered antigen, remains vague. In this study, we integrated physiological and metabolic phenotyping with intestinal transcriptomics, epithelial imaging, immune profiling, hepatic gene-expression analysis, and paired microbiome profiling to characterize the response to a single oral CTx exposure in mice. Within 24 h, CTx remodeled immune-cell composition in both epithelial and lamina propria compartments, with responses shaped by sex and genetic background. Recurrent changes included increased epithelial group 3 innate lymphoid cells, reduced lamina propria RORγt+ regulatory T cells, and decreased epithelial ILC1/NK cells in males of both strains. CTx also increased villus DCLK1+ tuft cells and reduced MUC2 immunoreactivity. Jejunal transcriptomics revealed induction of inflammatory defense, glycolytic, autophagy, and lipid-utilization programs together with suppression of proliferative and mitochondrial programs, consistent with coordinated stress adaptation. These local changes were accompanied by rapid restructuring of the fecal microbial community and by systemic hypometabolism, despite markedly different hypothermic responses across strains. CTx also elicited a selective hepatic stress and metabolic program, including conserved suppression of Cyp7a1 across sexes and strains. Together, these findings show that CTx alone rapidly reorganizes the intestinal immune, epithelial, metabolic, and microbial environment while suppressing whole-body metabolism. This work provides an integrated framework for understanding the acute host response to CTx and for interpreting its widespread use as a mucosal adjuvant.

paper.title: Ethmoid bone marrow region modulates lymphoid activation and differentiation with distinct myeloid profile in neuroinflammation.
paper.abstract: The skull bone marrow axis has recently emerged as an important source of immune cells during neuroinflammation, including in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), the mouse model of multiple sclerosis. The cribriform plate bone marrow (cpBM), is a portion of the ethmoid bone of the skull of mice, and is positioned next to nasal regions. At the cribriform plate olfactory nerves pass through the skull and recent evidence supports that it represents an important immune niche with links to CSF outflow and connections to cpBM. Previous data supports cellular composition of the ethmoid bone marrow in mice is altered in neuroinflammation suggesting it senses inflammatory cues, but the exact nature of these changes is still unclear. Here using scRNAseq and flow cytometry of the ethmoid bone marrow region we test how the region responds to EAE. In addition, we also compare the cpBM region with systemic bone marrow in the femur to understand region specific differences. We report that neuroinflammation creates a regulatory response at these sites and implicates the cpBM in controlling these effects. A better understanding of the cribriform niche may offer new treatments for neuroinflammatory disease.

paper.title: Cellular and molecular census of the pleiotropic disease locus Negr1 in zebrafish.
paper.abstract: A major challenge in precision medicine is to understand the cellular origin of disease-causing genetic alterations. One prominent example is the Negr1 locus , where common non-coding variants are associated with an unusually broad range of human traits and conditions, including body mass index (BMI), major depression, schizophrenia, autism-spectrum conditions and anorexia. Yet, no coding loss-of-function allele has been established as causal. These observations suggest that distinct Negr1 -expressing cell populations underlie distinct traits. However, this hypothesis is difficult to test in tractable experimental systems without first determining where this gene may act. To overcome this limitation, we generated a knock-in reporter at the zebrafish Negr1 locus and combined single-cell transcriptomics with whole-brain registration and single-neuron projection mapping. We found that Negr1 is expressed in a graded manner across neuronal classes of the brain and retina, radial glia and astrocyte-like cells, and most consistently in oligodendrocyte progenitor cells. Projection mapping suggests three conserved hubs formed by olfactory bulb projection neurons, tectal periventricular projection neurons and cerebellar eurydendroid cells. Our findings are consistent with the idea that Negr1 pleiotropy arises from dose perturbation of a rather broadly expressed gene. More generally, this integrative approach to produce granular multimodal datasets should enable high-resolution etiological studies in models of human disease.

paper.title: The chemosensory system of the clonal raider ant larva.
paper.abstract: Ant larvae are blind and immobile, depending heavily on the adults for care in the form of feeding, grooming, and transport. However, they are not inactive colony members but play a central role in the organization of ant societies by modulating adult behavior and physiology. While adult ants have been studied extensively, we still know little about what sensory modalities larvae use to perceive their environment. Here, we provide a molecular and circuit-level characterization of the chemosensory system of the clonal raider ant larva. Combining scanning electron microscopy and confocal imaging, we show that dome sensilla in the maxillary and labial palps are innervated by odorant receptor (OR) neurons. A larger population of ionotropic receptor (IR) neurons innervate papilla sensilla across various regions of the larval head: the antennae, the labrum, the maxillary palps and galeae, as well as the labial palps and the ventral labium. This suggests that IRs, which can have various functions, from taste and olfaction to temperature and humidity sensing, constitute the predominant chemosensory modality in ant larvae. To investigate projections into the central brain, we imaged transgenic lines that fluorescently label OR- and IR-expressing neurons. We found that OR- and IR-expressing neurons in the labium and maxilla project along the labial and maxillary nerves through the subesophageal ganglion to the deutocerebrum, whereas IR-expressing neurons from the labrum project to the tritocerebrum and those from the antenna project to the posterior deutocerebrum. Together, our findings establish a structural and molecular framework to study larval chemosensation in ants.

paper.title: Integrating airborne chemical ecology with informed intercropping for sustainable crop protection.
paper.abstract: The role of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in plant-insect interactions has been studied in detail in recent decades, especially in the context of environment-friendly integrated pest management (IPM) in agroecosystems. Field-based study and behavioural investigations have shown that specific VOCs (or combinations of VOCs) of companion crops are crucial in diverting phytophagous insects from main food or cash crops, along with attracting beneficial insects which decimate pest species. The functional mechanisms of these olfactory cues, however, are not always clear and distinctive, especially since these ecological interactions are highly variable. The complex 'odourscapes' occurring in mixed cropping systems are determined by species-specific interactions, local climate, prevalent agricultural/landscaping practices, and other environmental factors which need to be examined in localized contexts. This review aims to cover the dynamics and mechanisms of VOCs mediating plant-insect interactions in mixed crop settings, the variables and technical constraints to be considered for implementing these interactions for cost-effective IPM, and potential challenges presented by ecological fine-tuning of such interactions.

paper.title: Combining essential oils and kaolin clay increased repellency against Bemisia tabaci (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae): implications for management.
paper.abstract: The sweetpotato whitefly, Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius) (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae), is a major pest of vegetable crops worldwide. Management of this pest relies on insecticides, but overuse has led to resistance development and negative effects on non-target organisms. Repellent essential oils can be a sustainable alternative to insecticides. The residual efficacy of essential oils is relatively short, but combining them with kaolin clay provides enhanced repellency against whiteflies and a slower release rate. While many essential oils have been evaluated against whiteflies, most studies utilize different protocols, making comparisons between compounds challenging. In this study, 12 essential oils were screened against B. tabaci using a Y-tube olfactometer. Limonene, E-cinnamaldehyde, citral, cumin oil, and geraniol had a significant repellent effect on whiteflies, while the other oils did not. A dual-choice bioassay evaluated the significantly repellent oils, with and without kaolin clay, on whitefly-infested squash plants. Plants treated with E-cinnamaldehyde displayed phytotoxicity symptoms at the concentration tested. Among the remaining 4 compounds, citral applied alone repelled more whiteflies than limonene, geraniol, and an untreated control. Combining each oil with kaolin clay significantly improved their repellency compared to just the oil or kaolin alone. Combining limonene and kaolin was as effective as combining citral and kaolin despite citral being the most repellent compound on its own. This study demonstrates that kaolin clay has an additive effect for each oil tested, which may be used in an integrated pest management (IPM) program to extend the repellency duration against whiteflies in squash.

paper.title: Dorsal Crypsis and Chemical Defense Jointly Shape Brain Size in Toads.
paper.abstract: The cognitive benefits of having a large brain must outweigh its substantial energetic demands for such an organ to evolve. The cognitive buffer hypothesis proposes that large brains facilitate survival in complex environments via flexible behaviors. Because active predator evasion is likely more cognitively demanding than a cryptic lifestyle, we reasoned that the evolution of crypsis could relax selection on brain size. To test this hypothesis, we examined the effect of dorsal crypsis, ventral crypsis, and granular glands on relative total brain evolution in eight toad species. As predicted, total relative brain size was negatively associated with dorsal crypsis across species, but was not related to either the volume or the count of granular glands. Additionally, because certain brain regions may be specifically involved in predator evasion, we assessed relationships between five major brain region sizes and both dorsal crypsis and granular gland traits. Only the olfactory nerves and telencephalon showed negative associations with dorsal crypsis, whereas optic tectum volume correlated positively with granular gland volume. These regions support complex evasion strategies. Our findings indicate that increased dorsal crypsis relaxes selection on cognitively demanding evasion, leading to smaller brains. Thus, crypsis evolution is a previously underexplored factor in vertebrate brain anatomy evolution.

paper.title: Aroma-active compounds in brown butter.
paper.abstract: Brown butter has gained popularity as an ingredient, yet its flavor chemistry remains uncharacterized. This study characterized the aroma-active compounds and sensory properties of brown butter. Duplicate lots of salted and unsalted fresh butter were obtained from a manufacturer, and a standardized browning method was developed. Brown and unheated butters were evaluated by descriptive analysis and instrumental color analysis. Volatiles were extracted using headspace solid-phase microextraction and direct solvent extraction followed by solvent-assisted flavor evaporation and analyzed by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, gas chromatography-olfactometry, and gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Aroma extract dilution analysis, stable isotope dilution analysis, sensory threshold determination, odor activity values, and model systems were used to identify, quantify and determine key aroma contributors. Brown butter exhibited higher intensities of cooked-nutty, caramel, and brown-toasted flavors compared with unheated butters. Brown butter was characterized by browned color, Maillard reaction derived volatiles, lipid oxidation products, and select sulfur compounds, while other low molecular weight volatiles decreased. Furaneol, diacetyl, and 2-nonanone as well as other aldehydes, ketones, lactones and sulfur compounds were identified as key contributors to brown butter aroma. These findings provide a comprehensive chemical and sensory framework for understanding brown butter flavor development and highlight the importance of thermal processing conditions in shaping butter aroma and flavor through Maillard reaction and lipid degradation pathways.

paper.title: Effect of a Nutritional and Culinary Support Intervention on Food-Related Quality of Life During Chemotherapy.
paper.abstract:
CONTEXT: Chemotherapy adversely affects nutritional status and the eating experience in patients with cancer, yet its impact on food-related quality of life (QoL) remains underexplored. The CANUT guide was developed to provide practical nutritional, sensory, and culinary support during treatment. This study aims to evaluate the effect of the CANUT intervention on food-related QoL in patients undergoing chemotherapy. Secondary objectives included health-related QoL, dietary intake, and anthropometric and functional parameters.

METHOD: In this RCT, 209 patients with cancer receiving chemotherapy were randomly assigned (1:1) to an intervention group (dietary counselling supported by the CANUT guide) or control group (standard care). Food-related QoL was assessed using the ALT-QVA score, reflecting chemotherapy-related sensory alterations, meal experience, digestive discomfort, and adaptive dietary behaviours. Health-related QoL (EORTC QLQ-C30), dietary intake (24-hour recall), anthropometry, and handgrip strength were collected. Outcomes were measured at baseline and after four chemotherapy cycles. Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: Food-related QoL declined over time (-2.85±0.53, P<0.001), with no significant between-group difference (P=0.553). Exploratory analyses showed that the decline was significant in patients reporting taste and smell alterations and in smokers, highlighting the role of sensory changes and lifestyle factors in shaping the eating experience. Health-related QoL also decreased (-8.1±1.7, P<0.001), with no between-group difference (P=0.705). Energy and protein intake did not differ between groups, with >75% of patients below recommendations at both time points. Anthropometric and functional parameters remained unchanged.

CONCLUSION: The CANUT intervention did not improve food-related QoL or nutritional outcomes in a population mostly consisting of women with breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy. This highlights the need for more integrated, comprehensive, and multimodal strategies addressing sensory alterations and individual characteristics of patients during chemotherapy (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05027490).

paper.title: Management of Craniofacial Hyperhidrosis with Botulinum Toxin: A Systematic Review.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Treatment of craniofacial hyperhidrosis (CFH) is challenging because of the anatomical characteristics of the head and face. Although topical anticholinergics are generally considered first-line therapy, botulinum toxin has emerged as an effective option, while evidence remains more limited than for axillary hyperhidrosis. The objective of this study is to systematically review current evidence on the efficacy and safety of botulinum toxin in the treatment of CFH.

METHODS: Clinical studies evaluating different types of botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) and type B (BoNT-B) for CFH were reviewed, focusing on treatment efficacy, onset of response, anatomical sites and safety.

RESULTS: BoNT-A was the most consistently studied formulation and demonstrated substantial improvement of CFH. The duration of response generally ranged from 4 to 9 months, with more recent cohorts reporting efficacy lasting up to 12 months. Onset of action typically occurred within 1-2 weeks. The forehead and scalp were the most frequently treated sites, followed by gustatory and occipital regions. BoNT-B also produced significant reductions in sweating and improvements in quality of life.

CONCLUSION: Botulinum toxin appears to be an effective and safe treatment for CFH. Long-term studies are needed to establish the optimal toxin type, administration technique and retreatment interval.

paper.title: Phenology drives rice-fall armyworm interactions and arthropod community dynamics through foliar volatile signaling.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are one of the key mediators of plant-insect interactions. Although several studies have examined the factors affecting volatile-mediated tritrophic interactions, the role of phenology in determining the effects of volatile emission is less understood, especially in rice. Currently, fall armyworm (FAW, Spodoptera frugiperda) is considered a minor pest in rice; however, changes in climatic conditions and the rapid emergence of pesticide resistance can quickly alter this status. To address this, we examined how plant phenology and FAW herbivory affect foliar volatile emissions and the associated arthropod community dynamics in rice.

RESULTS: Among the phenological stages (n = 6 per treatment), the vegetative stage emitted significantly more day volatiles than the reproductive stage. FAW herbivory also induced volatile emission in rice. Furthermore, in the Y-tube olfactometer choice assays, FAW larvae preferred volatiles from the vegetative stage and undamaged plants. After normalizing volatile emissions by plant biomass, the most common volatile compounds emitted included diketone alcohol, ethylhexyl benzoate, and ethylhexanol. In the common garden experiment, more arthropods, regardless of their taxonomic status, were attracted to the vegetative stage, although they were not significantly attracted to FAW-damaged plants. In addition, Diptera was the most predominant order observed, irrespective of the treatments.

CONCLUSION: Our findings collectively show that phenology is the key driver in mediating volatile-mediated tritrophic interactions in rice. The observed phenology-driven changes in VOC emissions influence differences in arthropod attraction, suggesting ecological consequences in rice-FAW interactions and highlighting the importance of incorporating phenology into sustainable pest management strategies. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

paper.title: A kleptomyiophilous orchid exploits milichiid flies through mimicry of common pentatomoid bugs with high levels of toxicity.
paper.abstract: To attract pollinators, mimetic flowers imitate the visual and olfactory cues that their pollinators use when responding to models.1,2 However, it is unclear which processes influence the mimicry of particular models. One possibility is that selection favors mimicry of models that act as "magnet species" by attracting large numbers of potential pollinators.1,3,4,5 According to this hypothesis, models should be highly common, even if they are not the most attractive resources. This may apply to kleptomyiophilous flowers that exploit kleptoparasitic flies by imitating injured insects.6,7,8,9,10 In this form of mimicry, the injured insect models would be highly common, even if they emit toxic defensive volatiles that could impede pollinator activities.11,12 We report that the eastern ecotype of Bulbophyllum claviforme attracts a specific kleptoparasitic milichiid pollinator Phyllomyza sp. 1. Orchid floral scent is similar to (E)-2-decenal-dominated emissions of multiple pentatomoid bugs in the families Pentatomidae, Scutelleridae, Plataspidae, and Acanthosomatidae. Bioassays suggest that undecane, (E)-2-decenal and (E)-2-decenyl acetate are critical for attraction. Three (E)-2-alkenals, namely (E)-2-hexenal, (E)-2-octenal, and (E)-2-decenal, are both toxic and attractive to Phyllomyza sp. 1, with the toxicity of dominant (E)-2-alkenals negatively correlated to attractiveness. The orchid paradoxically appears to mimic pentatomoids that are less attractive due to higher toxicity. Selection may have favored mimicry of these bugs because (E)-2-decenal is emitted by a wide range of species, representing 68% of the pentatomoid species sampled. Our findings are congruent with the hypothesis that magnet species effects on pollinator abundance are important for the evolution of floral mimicry.
